app.title: SPC
app.subtitle: Statistical process control after AIAG-VDA SPC Manual (2026)
app.notice: Reference build: it follows the Yellow Volume draft (Feb 2026). Data, marks and reports are stored in the database and shared by all signed-in users.
import.title: Import a CSV file
import.intro: Choose a file, check the columns, then import. Excel files saved as CSV (UTF-8 or Big5) are read correctly.
import.missing_skip: Skip the row and note it
issue.encoding: The file cannot be decoded as UTF-8 or Big5.
issue.duplicate_header: Two columns have the same name.
issue.missing_column: A chosen column is not in the file.
issue.bad_number: The value is not a number. Check the decimal mark.
issue.bad_timestamp: The date and time is not in a known format.
issue.bad_flag: The valid flag is not understood.
issue.invalid_without_reason: A value marked invalid needs a reason.
issue.bad_source_row: The original row number is not a number.
issue.no_data: The file has no data rows.
data.title: Data and outliers
data.select_hint: Tick rows to mark or restore them.
data.suspects_note: A hint is not a reason. A test only shows that a value does not fit the assumed distribution. Mark a value only when you know why it cannot come from the process, for example a wrong measurement or a calibration part. Marked values stay in the data and are left out of all calculations.
data.suspects_found: {n} suspect value(s). They are highlighted in the table.
data.reason_hint: Why can this value not come from the investigated process?
analysis.title: Analysis
analysis.stage_production: Production: performance or capability (Pp/Ppk or Cp/Cpk)
analysis.subgroup_size: Subgroup size (for data without subgroup labels)
analysis.model_A2: A2: constant, not normal (for example roundness)
analysis.model_C3: C3: location trend (for example tool wear)
analysis.model_C4: C4: systematic and random (for example lot change)
analysis.model_hint: Only A1 and A2 are in statistical control. Without a model, results are named Pp/Ppk.
analysis.controlled_stable: The process is controlled stable: values stay inside the limits and well inside the tolerance, and operators monitor and adjust it by procedure.
analysis.mode_random_range: Allow the alarms that chance explains (draft)
analysis.rules_hint: Each extra criterion finds special causes sooner and also raises the false alarm rate. Switch on only what the process needs.
analysis.rule_run: Run on one side of the center line, points:
analysis.rule_middle_third: Middle third (25 points: fewer than 11 or more than 23 inside)
analysis.rule_two_of_three: 2 of 3 beyond 2 sigma on one side
analysis.rule_four_of_five: 4 of 5 beyond 1 sigma on one side
analysis.incomplete: Subgroups that lost values to invalid marks
analysis.incomplete_drop: Leave them out and list them
analysis.customer: Customer or parameter set name (kept with the result)
result.title: Result
result.no_spec_on_chart: Specification limits are not drawn on control charts.
result.class_not_tested: Not tested in a machine study
result.alarm_points: Alarm points: {n} of {k} points checked, {expected} expected by chance, {threshold} allowed
result.names_reason_machine: Machine performance study: stability is not tested.
result.names_reason_preliminary: Preliminary study: stability cannot be proven yet.
result.names_reason_stable: Stability is proven, so the capability name applies.
result.names_reason_not_proven: Stability is not proven, so the performance name applies.
result.target_adjusted: Targets are raised for the smaller sample.
result.target_blocked: A critical characteristic needs the full sample of {base}. No reduced target exists.
result.verdict_meets: Met, also at the lower confidence limit
result.verdict_meets_estimate_only: Estimate met, lower confidence limit below target
result.diagnosis_note: Cw/Cwk use only the variation inside subgroups. They are for analysis and must not go into reports. A Cwk far above Ppk or Cpk points to variation between subgroups.
warn.data_subgroup_not_contiguous: Subgroup {label} is not in one block in the file.
warn.data_time_not_ordered: The timestamps are not in time order. Subgroups follow the file order.
warn.data_rows_skipped: {count} row(s) with an empty value were skipped.
warn.attribute_small_sample: Sample size is at or below {limit}. Small changes may stay unseen.
warn.attribute_size_varies: Sample size varies by 25 % or more. Limits change from point to point.
warn.edition_final_unverified: The release edition rules were not checked against a primary source. Check the targets with the handbook.
warn.dropped_subgroups: {count} subgroup(s) were left out because values were marked invalid: {labels}.
warn.few_subgroups: Only {k} subgroups. The handbook asks for at least 25.
warn.sample_below_base: {n} values is below the base sample size {base}. Targets and intervals are less certain.
warn.named_pp_not_cp: Named Pp/Ppk because stability is not proven. Choose the time-dependent model to claim Cp/Cpk.
warn.spec_missing: No specification limit given. Only the control charts are shown.
warn.non_normal: The data do not look normal ({test}, p = {p_value}). These indices assume a normal distribution. Methods for non-normal data are not available yet.
warn.one_sided_no_p: One-sided specification: only the location index is given.
warn.target_not_allowed: No reduced target for a critical characteristic with {n} values. {base} are needed.
tools.title: Tools
tools.arl_max: Must be caught within this many subgroups (optional)
tools.arl_required: Smallest subgroup size that meets it
tools.arl_none: No subgroup size up to 1000 meets it.
error.import_failed: The file could not be imported.
error.incomplete_subgroups: {count} subgroup(s) lost values to invalid marks: {labels}. Allow leaving them out, or restore the values.
error.positions_out_of_range: Some selected rows do not exist.
error.already_invalid: Some selected values are already marked invalid.
error.not_invalid: Some selected values are not marked invalid.
error.dataset_not_found: This dataset does not exist (any more). It may have been deleted. Open another one under “Saved”.
error.file_too_large: The file is larger than {limit_mb} MB.
error.sizes_required: Sample sizes are required for this chart.
error.no_value_column: Choose the column with the measured values.
report.title: Report
report.intro: Make the 20+2 element report of this analysis. The report is a snapshot: later changes to the data do not change a report that already exists. The first fields fill the report elements 1 to 10 and 20 to 22.
report.persons: People who performed the study and measurements
report.period_text: Time of data collection (used when the data has no time stamps)
report.deviations: Deviations from stable operating conditions (environment, settings, cycle time)
report.sampling_frequency: Sampling frequency (used when the data has no time stamps)
report.uncertainty: Expanded measurement uncertainty U (for the guard band)
report.pdf_hint: To get a PDF, open the report and use the print function of the browser (A4).
report.needs_run: Run the analysis first. The report uses the same settings.
tools.archive_intro: Checks that the content was not changed and runs the calculation again from the stored data and parameters.
archive.integrity_bad: The content was changed after the archive was made (the digest does not match).
archive.reproduced_yes: The calculation gives the stored result again.
archive.reproduced_no: The calculation gives a different result:
archive.other_engine: The archive was made with another software version.
error.report_needs_spec: A report needs at least one specification limit.
error.archive_unreadable: The file is not a readable archive.
login.title: Sign in
login.setup_needed: No user exists yet. An administrator creates the first one on the server: spc-admin create-user NAME --role admin
login.session_ended: Your session has ended. Please sign in again.
password.title: Change password
password.forced: You must choose a new password before you can continue.
password.rules: At least {min} characters, not your user name.
password.done: Password changed. Your other sessions were signed out.
saved.title: Saved data and reports
saved.intro: Everything is stored in the database and shared by all users. Reports are snapshots and stay as they were made.
saved.confirm_delete: Delete dataset “{name}”? Reports made from it are kept.
admin.title: Administration
admin.reset_prompt: New temporary password for {name} (at least 10 characters):
admin.reset_done: Password of {name} was reset. They must change it at the next sign-in.
admin.unlocked: {name} can try to sign in again.
admin.created: User {name} created. They must change the password at the first sign-in.
admin.audit_note: Every sign-in, mark, report and user change is listed here and linked by a hash chain. A changed or removed entry breaks the chain. A cut-off end is only seen when you compare the last hash with one you kept elsewhere.
data.person_note: Marks are recorded under your sign-in: {user}.
error.csrf_failed: The request was refused for safety. Reload the page and sign in again.
error.forbidden: Your role is not allowed to do this. It needs the role: {role}.
error.invalid_credentials: User name or password is wrong.
error.login_locked: Too many wrong attempts. Try again in {minutes} min, or ask an administrator to unlock the name.
error.username_invalid: User names have 3–64 characters: letters, digits, . _ @ -
error.last_admin: This is the last active administrator. Make another one first.
error.password_unchanged: The new password must differ from the current one.
error.password_too_short: The password needs at least {min} characters.
error.password_too_long: The password may have at most {max} characters.
error.password_is_username: The password may not be the user name.
error.password_too_simple: The password is too simple. Use more different characters.
analysis.distribution_hint: For a normal distribution the indices use the total standard deviation. For other data, fit a distribution: the indices then come from its quantiles (.G) or from the shares outside the limits (.Z). Choose with knowledge of the process. Automatic choice only helps.
analysis.bootstrap: Bootstrap resamples for the interval (0 = no interval)
analysis.seed: Random seed of the bootstrap (kept with the result)
result.dist_boot: Interval: bootstrap, {used} of {requested} resamples used, seed {seed}.
result.dist_boot_failed: No interval: only {used} of {requested} resamples could be fitted.
result.dist_no_boot: No interval: the bootstrap is switched off. A target is judged on the estimate alone.
result.dist_cand_note: Smaller AIC fits better. AIC and Anderson-Darling describe the fit. They are no pass/fail tests, because the parameters come from the same data. A normal distribution within 2 AIC units of the best wins the automatic choice.
result.dist_ranked_sample: The families were ranked on a random sample of {n} values. The chosen one was fitted on all values.
warn.bootstrap_failed: The interval could not be computed: only {succeeded} of {requested} resamples could be fitted. The target is judged on the estimate alone.
warn.fit_small_sample: Only {n} values: the tail quantiles (0.135 % and 99.865 %) of a fitted distribution are extrapolated and uncertain.
data.restart_note: After a tool change or an action that followed an alarm, the moving characteristics of an I-MR chart must start again. Otherwise the old values cause more alarms although the process is corrected. Select the first value after the event and give the reason above. A moving range never spans a restart. The restart is stored with your sign-in.
data.restart_list: Restarts before the values with No.: {rows}
analysis.moving_hint: 1 = individual values. A larger size plots moving means. After the start and after every restart the size grows 1, 2, … up to this value, so there is no blind spot.
result.moving_line: Individuals chart with moving sample size {n} and {k} restart(s) (dotted lines). The limits follow the size of the moving sample.
warn.restarts_not_used: {n} restart(s) in the data are not used. Only the I-MR chart restarts.
warn.restart_without_effect: {n} restart(s) have no effect: there is no valid value before or after them in the data used.
error.restart_at_start: A restart before the first value has no effect.
error.already_restart: There is a restart before this value already.
error.not_restart: There is no restart before this value.
data.restart_phase: New limits from here: the process was changed on purpose. The centre line and the limits are calculated again from the values after this point. Leave it off when the process is the same and only the moving sample must start again.
result.phase_line: Phase {k}, from file row {from}: {n} values, centre line {mu}, σ̂ {sigma}
analysis.profile_hint: A profile fixes the settings that the customer agreed on: they are applied by the program and cannot be changed here. The report then uses the layout of the profile.
analysis.profile_line: Profile {name}, revision {rev}. Fixed by the profile: {keys}.
report.extra_title: Information required by the customer profile
admin.profiles_note: A profile holds the analysis settings and the report layout of one customer. Everybody can use a profile. Only administrators change them. A change raises the revision number. A report keeps its own copy of the profile it used.
admin.profile_confirm_delete: Delete the customer profile “{name}”? Reports that were made with it keep their own copy.
admin.pf_analysis: Analysis settings fixed by the customer agreement
admin.pf_blank: Leave a field empty to keep the program's default.
admin.pf_alpha: Risk α of the control limits (two-sided)
admin.pf_est: Confidence of the interval of an index
admin.pf_targets: Target values (p and pk) per stage and characteristic class. Empty cells keep the draft's example values. Give both numbers of a cell.
admin.pf_logo: Logo (PNG or JPEG, at most 150 KB)
admin.pf_lang_any: As chosen when the report is made
admin.pf_el22: Show element 22 (measurement uncertainty and guard band)
admin.pf_required: Fields that the author must fill
admin.pf_extra: Extra fields of the customer (asked when the report is made)
error.profile_not_found: This customer profile does not exist (any more).
error.profile_name_taken: A customer profile with this name exists already.
error.report_field_required: The customer profile requires these fields: {fields}
error.report_field_unknown: These extra fields do not belong to the customer profile: {fields}
error.profile_targets_pair: Give both targets of a cell (p and pk), or leave both empty.
mon.title: SPC at the line (control loop 1)
mon.intro: An SPC monitor controls the process directly. Its limits are fixed. Every new sample is checked at once, and every violation must be followed by the out-of-control action plan. Specification limits are not part of this chart.
mon.alerts_line: Open incidents: {open} (not yet taken over: {unack}, overdue: {overdue})
mon.f_warn: Risk of the warning limits (empty = no warning limits)
mon.f_source: Where the first limits come from
mon.src_sigma: Standard deviation of the individual values
mon.specs_note: The chart at the line never shows these limits. They are used for the ongoing report, which belongs to the higher control loops.
mon.f_rules: Stability criteria besides the control limits
mon.ocap_note: What the operator does when a criterion is violated, who is responsible, and who is called when nothing helps. A criterion without its own row uses the default row. A change of the plan has to be confirmed again by everybody.
mon.f_require_ack: Everybody must confirm that they know the action plan before entering samples
mon.ack_needed: You have not yet confirmed that you know the action plan. This is the plan:
mon.label: Label (lot, part no.)
mon.result_ok: Sample {seq}: within the limits. Go on.
mon.result_warning: Sample {seq}: inside the control limits, but beyond a warning limit. Watch the next samples.
mon.result_alarm: Sample {seq}: OUT OF CONTROL. Follow the action plan.
mon.verification_note: This sample was taken during an open incident. It counts as verification.
mon.next_step: First measure again or take a second sample to make sure that the sample is valid.
mon.no_spec_note: Specification limits are not shown here on purpose: at the line the control limits count.
mon.invalidate_prompt: Why is sample {seq} invalid (for example: gauge not zeroed)?
mon.not_taken_over: nobody has taken it over yet
mon.overdue: OVERDUE: not escalated {min} minutes after the violation
mon.outcome_recovered: control is back (needs a new sample that meets all criteria)
mon.outcome_escalated: handed to the root cause analysis
mon.limits_now: Limits revision {rev}. Mean {mu}, standard deviation {sigma}. Lower limit / centre / upper limit:
mon.new_limits_note: Do this when the process location or variation changed through control or improvement, or when the review says the limits do not fit. The limits stay fixed afterwards. The criteria start again from the next sample.
mon.ongoing_note: The index of the latest samples, calculated like an analysis chart. Stability decides whether it is called performance or capability. Here the specification limits are used.
mon.ongoing_report: Make a report of this window
mon.og_targets: Targets: p {p}, pk {pk}. Verdict for pk: {verdict}
mon.og_no_spec: The monitor has no specification limits, so no index is given.
mon.quadrant_2: Quadrant II: performing but not stable
mon.quadrant_3: Quadrant III: stable but the targets are missed
mon.quadrant_4: Quadrant IV: not stable and the targets are missed
mon.quadrant_unknown: No quadrant: there are no targets to judge by (give the characteristic class and the limits).
mon.quadrant_note: Quadrants I to IV follow figure 10-26 of the draft. Only I fulfils stability and capability.
mon.review_ok: The limits fit the data (spread {ratio} times the spread behind the limits, {alarms} alarm samples, {expected} expected).
mon.review_too_narrow: The limits look too narrow (spread {ratio} times the spread behind the limits, {alarms} alarm samples, {expected} expected). Too narrow limits cause over-regulation. Consider new limits.
mon.review_too_wide: The limits look too wide (spread {ratio} times the spread behind the limits). Real changes may stay unnoticed. Consider new limits.
mon.review_location_moved: The location has moved by {shift} standard errors from the centre line. If this is the new normal, set new limits with a reason.
mon.og_response: Response of the action plan: {n} incidents ({open} open, {overdue} overdue). Median time to take over: {ack}, to the first action: {action}, to close: {close}.
error.wrong_value_count: This monitor takes {n} value(s) per sample. Fill them all in.
error.ocap_not_acknowledged: Confirm first that you know the action plan of this monitor.
error.no_limits: This monitor has no limits yet.
error.bad_time: The time of the sample is not a date and time.
error.time_in_future: The time of the sample lies in the future.
error.bad_source: The source of the limits cannot be used: {message}
error.monitor_shape_locked: The chart type, the sample size and the risk cannot change. Make a new monitor, or set new limits.
error.text_required: Write what was done, or the result.
error.already_acknowledged: Somebody has taken this over already.
error.sample_still_valid: Declare the sample invalid on its row first, with a reason.
error.verification_missing: Enter a new sample after the last action. It must meet all criteria.
error.escalation_missing: Log the escalation or the start of the root cause analysis first.
error.not_enough_points: There are not enough valid samples yet (at least 10).
error.monitor_not_found: This monitor does not exist (any more).
error.monitor_name_taken: A monitor with this name exists already.
result.kind_p: p chart – share of nonconforming units
result.kind_np: np chart – number of nonconforming units
mon.src_rate_value: Reference level (p-bar for p and np, per unit for c and u)
mon.src_counts_list: Counts of at least 20 reference samples, separated by spaces or commas
mon.src_sizes_list: Sample sizes of the same samples, in the same order
mon.limits_now_count: Limits revision {rev}. Reference level {center}. Lower limit / centre line / upper limit of the latest sample:
mon.limits_per_size: The limits are exact (binomial or Poisson) and follow the size of each sample.
error.report_not_for_attribute: Counts have no capability report: it needs measured values.
result.kind_acc-x: Acceptance chart – individual values and moving range
result.kind_pre: Pre-control chart – worst part of each pair
alarmrule.pre_two_yellow_same_side: Two parts in the yellow zone on the same side
alarmrule.pre_two_yellow_opposite: Two parts in the yellow zones on opposite sides
mon.src_tolerance_note: The zones come from the tolerance alone: green is the middle half, yellow the outer quarters, red is outside.
mon.f_accept_p: Accepted fraction out of tolerance p (%)
mon.f_accept_pa: Probability of intervention P_A when p is reached (%)
mon.limits_now_pre: Limits revision {rev}. Zones of the tolerance: red outside, yellow in the outer quarters, green in the middle half. Lower limit / middle / upper limit:
mon.limits_accept: Limits revision {rev}. Acceptance chart: factor k = {k} for p = {p} % and P_A = {pa} %; within standard deviation {sigma} = {ratio} of the tolerance. Lower limit / target / upper limit:
mon.accept_variation_warning: The variation is more than one tenth of the tolerance. The draft expects a standard deviation of at most T/10 for an acceptance chart: reduce the variation or use a process related chart.
mon.qualified: Released: the last {greens} parts are in the green zone (at least {needed} are needed).
mon.not_qualified: Not yet released: {greens} of {needed} consecutive parts in the green zone.
mon.pre_note: A pre-control chart only monitors a start-up from the tolerance. It does not control a process: use it only until process related limits exist. The draft gives no rules for it; these are the classical ones.
error.report_not_for_precontrol: A pre-control chart has no capability report: it only monitors a start-up.
result.kind_cusum: CUSUM chart – upper (CO) and lower (CU) cumulative sum
result.kind_ewma: EWMA chart – exponentially weighted moving average
alarmrule.shift_up: Upward shift of the mean detected
alarmrule.shift_down: Downward shift of the mean detected
mon.f_cusum_k: Reference value k (shift to detect, in standard errors of the mean)
mon.f_cusum_fir: Head start as a share of h (0 = none; 0.5 = fast initial response)
mon.seq_note: A chart with memory finds small, lasting shifts of the mean. Large jumps it finds more slowly than a Shewhart chart: run an X-bar monitor next to it (draft 10.3.5.5). It assumes a stable variation. The chart starts again from its reference state after every signal.
mon.limits_cusum: Limits revision {rev}. CUSUM with target {mu}, standard deviation {sigma}, k = {k}, decision interval h = {h} (head start {fir}), average run length when in control {arl0}. Lower limit / zero / upper limit of the sums:
mon.limits_ewma: Limits revision {rev}. EWMA with target {mu}, standard deviation {sigma}, lambda = {lam}, L = {L}, average run length when in control {arl0}. Lower limit / target / upper limit once the chart has run in:
mon.arl_by_shift: Average run length by shift of the mean (in standard errors): {table}
mon.cusum_restart_note: The values shown are the upper sum CO (blue) and the lower sum CU (purple). After a signal both start again at their starting value.
mon.ewma_limits_note: The limits are narrower at the start and widen with every sample until they reach the values above. The run lengths in the table are for the wide limits, so a shift right at the start is found a little sooner. After a signal the chart starts again at the target.
result.kind_zmr: Short run Z-MR chart – values standardised per product
result.kind_t2: Hotelling T² chart – several characteristics together
mon.src_parts_list: One product per line: code; target; standard deviation (from earlier runs, a similar product or the process capability)
mon.src_observations_rows: One observation per line, one value per characteristic, separated by spaces or commas (at least 20, and 3 per characteristic)
mon.mv_names: Names of the characteristics, separated by commas (optional)
mon.mv_mu: Target of each characteristic, separated by commas
mon.mv_cov: Covariance matrix, one row per line
mon.src_text_vector: given target and covariance of {p} characteristics
mon.limits_zmr: Limits revision {rev}. Z-MR chart for {n} products: every value is standardised with the target and standard deviation of its product, so one set of limits serves all. Lower limit / centre / upper limit:
mon.limits_t2: Limits revision {rev}. Hotelling T² of {p} characteristics ({names}) with target {target}, given covariance. Upper limit {ucl} (chi-square, in-control run length {arl0}); there is no lower limit.
mon.limits_t2_estimated: Limits revision {rev}. Hotelling T² of {p} characteristics ({names}); target and covariance estimated from {n} observations, the limit allows for that. Upper limit {ucl} (in-control run length {arl0}); there is no lower limit.
mon.limits_mewma_mv: Limits revision {rev}. MEWMA of {p} characteristics ({names}), lambda = {lam}, target {target}. Upper limit h = {ucl} for an in-control run length of {arl0}; there is no lower limit.
mon.mewma_simulated_note: The limit h has no formula: it comes from a simulation of the run length (about 2 % uncertain in the run length). Estimates from observations are treated as known.
mon.mv_detail: Which characteristics carry the signal (z = standardised deviation of the sample mean; share = what T² loses without that characteristic): {list}
mon.zmr_note: Short runs: pick the product, then enter the measured value. The chart shows the standardised value (value − target) / standard deviation of that product. Adding a product needs new limits, and the criteria then start again.
mon.mv_note: Several characteristics: enter m rows of one value per characteristic. The chart signals when the combination is unusual, even if every value alone is within its range. The signal does not say which characteristic is the cause: see the shares.
error.part_required: Choose the product of this measurement.
error.unknown_part: Product {part} is not in the table of this monitor. Add it with new limits.
error.report_not_for_this_chart: This chart has no capability report: its values are not one independent series of one characteristic.
analysis.chart_ext-xbar: Shewhart chart with extended limits (mean and s)
mon.f_sigma_out: Standard deviation between the subgroups (sigma out)
mon.f_u_out: u out (1.5 is the usual empirical value)
mon.ext_method_anova: Analysis of variance: mean ± u in σ in/√n ± u out · σ out
mon.ext_method_extremes: Mean of the 3 largest and 3 smallest subgroup means
mon.f_kurt: Kurtosis of the plotted values (3 = normal)
mon.f_sigma_within: Standard deviation within a sample (empty = from the plotted values)
mon.pear_method_pearson: Pearson curve of skewness and kurtosis (Clements, ISO 22514-4)
mon.shape_note_ext: For processes whose mean is expected to move (tool wear, several machines). Standard deviation = within a sample; the limits are widened by the variation between the samples. Needs 30 or more subgroups to estimate from data.
mon.shape_note_pearson: For skewed processes. Mean and standard deviation are those of the plotted values (the sample means when n > 1). The limits are the 0.135 % and 99.865 % quantiles of a skewed curve, so they are not equally far from the centre. Needs 30 or more plotted values to estimate from data. Only the limits, runs and trends apply.
mon.limits_ext: Extended limits ({method}): σ within {sin}, σ between {sout}, u in = {uin}, u out = {uout}.
mon.limits_pearson: Limits from {method}: skewness {g1}, kurtosis {b2}, standard deviation of the plotted values {s}, curve {curve}.
analysis.chart_ar: Residual chart of an autoregressive model (autocorrelated values)
analysis.chart_multistream: Several streams (spindles, cavities): level and single stream
result.kind_ar: AR residual chart – deviation of each value from its forecast
result.kind_multistream: Several streams – mean over the streams and largest stream deviation
result.series_variation_multistream: Largest standardised deviation of a stream
mon.f_phi: Coefficients of the autoregressive model, separated by commas (phi 1, phi 2 ...). The standard deviation above is that of the residuals, the mean is the level of the values
mon.f_stream_names: Names of the streams, separated by commas (optional)
mon.f_stream_offsets: Fixed difference of each stream from the mean, separated by commas (empty = none)
mon.f_stream_sigma_time: Standard deviation of the common level between samples (batches, time)
mon.dep_note_ar: For values that follow each other closely (high-speed, automated processes). Each value is compared with the forecast of an autoregressive model of the earlier values, and the residual is charted. A slow drift that the model follows is not an alarm; a jump is. A lasting shift is absorbed by the model after some samples. The first values after the start use the level as the earlier values.
mon.dep_note_ms: For processes with several streams (spindles, cavities, heads): enter one value per stream, in the same order every time. The level chart shows the mean over the streams. The stream chart shows the largest deviation of one stream after the fixed difference between the streams and the common level are taken out. Estimating from data needs at least 20 rows.
mon.limits_ar: Limits revision {rev}. Autoregressive model of order {order}: coefficients {phi}, level {mu}, standard deviation of the residuals {sigma}. Residual limits: lower / zero / upper:
mon.limits_ar_diag: Reference: lag-1 autocorrelation {lag1}; Ljung-Box p of the residuals {p} (large = no autocorrelation left); standard deviation of the values {raw}, of the residuals {resid}.
mon.limits_ms: Limits revision {rev}. {k} streams, level {mu}, standard deviation within the streams {sw}, of the common level {st}. Largest stream deviation: limit h = {h}. Limits of the level chart: lower / centre / upper:
mon.stream_detail: Streams (z = deviation from the mean over the streams and from the stream's own offset, in standard deviations): {list}
mon.limits_mcusum_mv: Limits revision {rev}. MCUSUM (Crosier) of {p} characteristics ({names}), k = {k}, target {target}. Decision limit h = {ucl} for an in-control run length of {arl0}; there is no lower limit. After a signal the sum starts again at zero.
study.title: Machine performance studies (draft 8.1 to 8.3)
study.intro: A machine performance study checks a machine with parts made one after the other under repeatable conditions. This checklist follows chapters 8.1 to 8.3 of the draft: what must be prepared, how the study is run and what has to be checked in the data. Items that can be read from the data are evaluated automatically. A study can be closed when no item is open or failed; a recorded deviation passes but stays flagged.
study.f_specs: Specification (for the pre-production run and the centre)
study.natural_lsl: The lower limit is natural (such as 0)
study.f_sample: Number of parts and tool wear
study.f_reduced_by: Reduced number of parts approved by (name, customer)
study.f_reduced_reason: Why 50 parts are not possible (parts, time, measuring)
study.f_cycles: Dressing cycles covered by the sample
study.f_pre_five: Values of the 5 part run, separated by commas
study.verdict_ready: All items are settled. {flagged} item(s) carry a remark or a recorded deviation. The study can be closed.
study.verdict_blocked: {n} item(s) are open or failed: the study cannot be closed yet.
study.close_reason: Statement for closing the study (what was checked)
error.study_closed: The study is closed. Reopen it with a reason first.
error.note_required: A note is required: say why this does not apply, or what was agreed.
error.study_not_ready: The study cannot be closed: items are still open or failed.
error.study_name_taken: A study with this name exists already.
error.unknown_item: There is no such checklist item.
study.item.human: HuMan: the operator or technician stays the same during the study
study.item.material_constant: Material: batch, manufacturer and pre-processing are kept constant
study.item.method: Method: warm-up time, tool life and production flow are kept constant
study.item.milieu: Milieu: vibration, temperature, humidity and air pressure are controlled
study.item.machine_parameters: Machine parameters that are not fixed yet (cycle time, coolant flow, speed, infeed, pressure) are kept constant
study.item.changes_documented: Every change of an influence, even a single one such as a change of operator, is documented
study.item.deviations_agreed: Deviations from the specified conditions are agreed between customer and supplier and written in the order
study.item.sample_size: Number of parts: usually 50. Fewer only with an agreed minimum and the approval of the customer
study.item.tool_wear_cycles: High tool wear (grinding, honing): the sample covers at least 1.5 dressing cycles
study.item.material_homogeneous: All material meets the specification and is as homogeneous as possible for the characteristic (one batch, one line, one coil)
study.item.msa_evidence: Proof of capability exists for every measurement process and system (AIAG MSA, VDA 5): the MSA gate of the linked measurement system
study.item.warmed_up: The equipment has reached its operating temperature (thermal behaviour recorded until it is stable)
study.item.tools_conditioned: The tools have made several parts already: the study does not start with new tools
study.item.uninterrupted: Production runs without interruption under standard conditions. After an interruption the study is repeated
study.item.adjusted_to_center: The equipment is adjusted so that the values lie as close as possible to the middle of the tolerance
study.item.preproduction_1: Pre-production run, 1 part: within ±12.5 % of the tolerance centre (one-sided with a natural limit: within 62.5 % of the tolerance)
study.item.preproduction_5: Pre-production run, 5 parts: the mean as for 1 part and the range below 25 % of the tolerance
study.item.stations: Each station, clamping device or cavity is a study of its own (several cavities: also between and within the cavities)
study.item.traceability: Data are traceable: the production and the collection sequence are documented, so that a time line can be drawn
study.item.parts_retained: Test parts are kept until the acceptance of the machine (non-destructive tests) and blocked until the final acceptance
study.item.qualitative_stability: The value curve was assessed: no outliers and no patterns (jumps, steps, trends) without a reason. Otherwise remove the cause and repeat the study
study.item.distribution: The statistical distribution was evaluated as in 7.8.1
study.res.sample_size.warn: {n} parts, fewer than {needed}: reduced with approval (the targets for the indices rise, see 8.4)
study.res.sample_size.fail: {n} parts, fewer than {needed}, and the record has no approval with a reason
study.res.tool_wear_cycles.fail: needs at least {needed} dressing cycles covered; entered: {cycles}
study.res.tool_wear_cycles.not_needed: not a process with high tool wear
study.res.adjusted_to_center.pass: the mean is {share} % of the tolerance away from the centre (limit {limit} %)
study.res.adjusted_to_center.warn: the mean is {share} % of the tolerance away from the centre (usual limit {limit} %): adjust the machine
study.res.adjusted_to_center.not_needed: one-sided or incomplete specification: not evaluated
study.res.preproduction_5.pass: mean {loc} in the area {lo} to {hi}, range {range} below {rlim}
study.res.preproduction_5.fail: mean {loc} (area {lo} to {hi}) and range {range} (limit {rlim}): not both within the limits
study.res.stations.warn: name the station, clamping device or cavity of this study
study.res.traceability.warn: no time stamps: only the row order shows the sequence
study.res.data_numeric.pass: all {n_total} values are numbers and none is marked invalid
study.res.unknown.no_dataset: link a data set to the study
study.res.unknown.dataset_missing: the linked data set no longer exists
study.res.unknown.specs_incomplete: enter the specification limits in the study
study.res.unknown.no_test: the distribution test could not be run
tm.suggest: Suggest the model from the data
tm.hints: What I know about the process (optional)
tm.hints_note: The data decide first. What you tick here is only compared with the result: if it does not fit, the suggestion becomes less certain and you are told.
tm.hint_natural_limit: The characteristic has a natural limit (flatness, runout, roughness)
tm.hint_different_fixtures: Different centring of fixtures or workholding
tm.hint_tool_wear_trend: Tool wear with a trend, or a cycle
tm.hint_tool_or_batch_changes: Tool changes or changes of batch
tm.hint_spindle_wear: Different wear of spindles, equal centring
tm.not_enough: Not enough data for a suggestion: {k} subgroups, at least {min} subgroups and {values} values are needed.
tm.grouping_blocks: The data have no subgroups: blocks of {n} consecutive values were used ({k} blocks). That makes the suggestion less certain.
tm.reason_not_normal_unimodal: the distribution is not normal but has one mode
tm.reason_random_remainder: and varies at random around the trend (lot to lot)
tm.reason_random_location: the location changes at random, without a trend
tm.reason_instantaneous_not_normal: the values within a subgroup are not normal
tm.ev_location: Location: analysis of variance p = {anova}; the spread between the subgroups is {ratio} times the spread within; trend p = {trend}, a straight line explains {r2} of the variation of the subgroup means; p after the trend is taken out: {after}.
tm.ev_variation: Variation: dispersion test p = {disp}, the spread of the variances is {ratio} times what the shape of the data explains; largest to smallest subgroup standard deviation: {sd}.
tm.ev_shape: Shape: normality p within the subgroups = {inst}, of all values = {res}; modes: {modes}; skewness {skew}, kurtosis {kurt}.
tm.alternatives: With a looser or stricter limit for the tests, the data would also fit: {list}.
tm.hint_disagrees: Your hint "{hint}" points to {models}, not to this suggestion: look at the process again before you choose.
tm.implication_control: Only A1 and A2 are in statistical control: the indices are named Cp and Cpk only for a stable process.
tm.implication_no_control: This model is not in statistical control. Cp and Cpk may be used only if the process is controlled stable (draft 9.4): the study must show it and the line must monitor the characteristic.
msa.title: Measurement systems and the MSA gate
msa.intro: The draft assumes that the measurement process is capable and stable, and asks for the proof (VDA 5, AIAG MSA, ISO 22514-7). A measurement system holds that proof: resolution, tolerance and the studies (gauge R&R, type 1, stability of a reference). The gate checks it. A monitor, a machine study or a report that is tied to a system is stopped when the gate is blocked, and flagged when it is conditional. The expanded uncertainty and the guard band of the studies go into the report.
msa.f_resolution: Resolution of the display or the increment
msa.f_tolerance: Tolerance T (upper minus lower limit) of the characteristic
msa.policy_note: The draft gives no criteria of its own. The defaults are the usual ones of VDA 5 and AIAG MSA; they belong to the system and are part of the audit trail.
msa.p_validity: Months a gauge R&R study is valid
msa.p_stability_months: Months between checks of the reference (stability)
msa.p_resolution: Largest resolution in % of the tolerance
msa.p_grr_pass: Gauge R&R, capable up to (% of the tolerance)
msa.p_grr_conditional: Gauge R&R, conditional up to (% of the tolerance)
msa.p_cg: Smallest Cg and Cgk of a type 1 study
msa.p_guard: Error probability of the guard band (%)
msa.p_ucal: Standard uncertainty of the calibration of the reference
msa.p_require_stability: A stability check of a reference is required
msa.data_grr: One part per line. Operators are separated by a semicolon, the trials of an operator by spaces. Example for 3 operators with 2 trials: 0.29 0.41 ; 0.08 0.25 ; 0.04 -0.11 (at least 5 parts, 2 operators, 2 trials)
msa.data_type1: The repeated measurements of the reference standard, separated by spaces (at least 25, 50 are usual)
msa.data_stability: Measurements of a reference over time, in the order they were made, separated by spaces (at least 20)
msa.status_pass: The gate is open: the measurement process is proven.
msa.status_conditional: The gate is conditional: it passes with remarks. Work goes on, and is flagged.
msa.status_block: The gate is blocked: a monitor, study or report tied to this system is stopped until the proof is there or a waiver is recorded.
msa.waive_prompt: Waive the check "{check}": what was agreed, and with whom?
msa.res.resolution.pass: the resolution is {share} % of the tolerance (limit {limit} %)
msa.res.resolution.fail: the resolution is {share} % of the tolerance, above the limit of {limit} %: the gauge is too coarse
msa.res.resolution.missing: enter the resolution and the tolerance of the system
msa.res.grr.pass: gauge R&R {pct} % of the {basis}, ndc {ndc}: capable
msa.res.grr.warn: gauge R&R {pct} % of the {basis}, ndc {ndc}: conditional
msa.res.grr.fail: gauge R&R {pct} % of the {basis}, ndc {ndc}: not capable
msa.res.validity.pass: the gauge R&R is valid until {until}
msa.res.validity.fail: the gauge R&R was valid until {until}: repeat it
msa.res.stability.pass: no signal in the reference measurements; the next check is due by {until}
msa.res.stability.fail.signals: {signals} signal(s) in the reference measurements: the measurement process is not stable
msa.res.stability.fail.expired: the last check of the reference is older than the interval (it was due by {until})
msa.res.stability.missing: no check of a reference over time
msa.uncertainty: Expanded uncertainty U = {U} (k = {k}, standard uncertainty {u}); guard band {g} for an error probability of {risk} % (from gauge R&R study {study}). Acceptance limits are the specification limits moved inward by the guard band.
msa.uncertainty_note: Simplified: the gauge R&R, the bias of a type 1 study, the resolution and the calibration of the reference are combined as independent parts. It goes into the report (element 22) unless the author enters their own value.
msa.sum_grr: {n}: gauge R&R {pct} % of the {basis}, ndc {ndc}; repeatability {ev}, reproducibility {av}
msa.monitor_conditional: The measurement system {name} passes the gate with remarks. This sample is accepted and flagged.
error.msa_gate_blocked: The measurement system {system} is not proven. Complete the gauge R&R, stability and resolution checks, or record a waiver.
error.msa_system_missing: The measurement system of this monitor no longer exists.
error.msa_system_not_found: This measurement system does not exist.
error.msa_system_name_taken: A measurement system with this name exists already.
study.res.msa_evidence.pass: measurement system {system}: the gate is open
study.res.msa_evidence.warn: measurement system {system}: the gate is conditional, with remarks
study.res.msa_evidence.fail: measurement system {system}: the gate is blocked
study.res.unknown.no_system: link a measurement system to the study (or record a deviation with the reason)
study.res.unknown.system_missing: the linked measurement system no longer exists
plan.title: Control plan
plan.intro: A control plan lists, for each process step, what is controlled, how, how often, who reacts and which measurement system and chart are used (draft 6.7). It is released when every line is complete and the four planning roles have approved this revision.
plan.approvals_note: Each approval is bound to the revision it was given for. Any change to the plan clears them. Only a person who holds the SPC role can give its approval.
plan.verdict_ready: All lines are complete and approved: it can be released.
plan.chk.specification.fail: a product characteristic needs a specification limit
plan.chk.monitor.fail.monitor_missing: the monitor does not exist any more
plan.chk.reaction.pass.monitor: taken from the reaction plan of the monitor
plan.chk.msa.fail.system_missing: the measurement system does not exist any more
plan.chk.msa.warn.not_needed: a system is linked although no measurement is planned
plan.chk.uncertainty.pass: U = {U} ({share} % of the tolerance), guard band {guard_band}
plan.chk.uncertainty.fail: U = {U}: the guard bands leave no room in the tolerance {tolerance}
plan.chk.system_tolerance.warn: the tolerance of the system ({system}) differs from the line ({line})
roles.title: SPC roles and competencies
roles.intro: Table 6-1 of the draft: which competence each SPC role needs. SPC roles are separate from the login roles; one person can hold several. The planning roles approve control plans.
roles.key: – none · Basic · Expert. The last row counts the active people who hold the role and meet the table.
roles.prompt_note: How was it shown (training, test, experience)?
roles.resp_quality_planning: Plans the quality assurance, sets the SPC strategy and approves the control plan.
roles.resp_product_developer: Names the critical product characteristics and their specifications.
roles.resp_process_planner: Plans the process and the critical process parameters; approves the control plan.
roles.resp_inspection_planner: Plans measurement and inspection, the measurement systems and the sampling.
roles.resp_equipment_procurer: Specifies and accepts equipment with its capability requirements.
roles.resp_line_supervisor: Makes sure the charts are used and the reactions are followed.
roles.resp_line_operator: Takes the samples, plots the points and reacts to signals.
error.role_not_held: You do not hold this SPC role. An administrator or engineer assigns it first.
error.plan_not_ready: The plan is not complete or not approved by all roles.
error.plan_not_found: This control plan does not exist.
error.plan_name_taken: A control plan with this name exists already.
val.title: Verification and validation of the software (draft 11.2)
val.intro: IATF 16949 asks for verification and validation of analysis software. A run executes the built-in checks (the calculations against published tables and formulas from outside this program) and your reference cases (your data, your settings, results you expect from a named source). The record is kept with a digest and an HTML report.
val.cases: Reference cases (validation for the intended use)
val.cases_note: A case is the proof that the software gives the results you expect for your use. The examples of ISO/TR 11462-3 can be entered here: the data is sold with the standard.
val.f_values: Values (separated by blanks, commas or new lines)
val.f_expected_note: Each line: path in the result, value, relative tolerance. Example: indices.pk 1.2345 0.000001. Paths: indices.p, indices.pk, indices.mean, indices.sd, chart.location.ucl, indices.ci_p.0 ...
val.bad_settings: The other settings are not valid JSON.
error.validation_case_not_found: This reference case does not exist.
error.validation_case_name_taken: A reference case with this name exists already.
error.validation_run_not_found: This validation run does not exist.
eq.title: Equipment interface: OPC UA (draft 11.1)
eq.intro: Measured values go from the machine to the monitors without typing. A link names an OPC UA server and the nodes that feed monitors. It is enabled only after a test read of exactly this configuration in which every node came back as a number with good quality and a timestamp. Readings are entered in the name of the person who enabled the link, who must know the action plan of the monitors.
eq.runner_on: The OPC UA client is running.
eq.runner_off: The OPC UA client is not running: start the server with the OPC UA option installed (pip install 'spc[opcua]'). Links can be set up and tested, but enabled links do not read.
eq.f_nodes_note: Each line: node id, monitor number, scale, offset. The value on the chart is value × scale + offset. Example: ns=2;s=Station1.Bore 1 0.001 0. The subgroup size of the monitor decides how many readings make one point. The password itself is never stored.
error.equipment_link_not_found: This equipment link does not exist.
error.equipment_name_taken: A link with this name exists already.
error.equipment_not_tested: Run a test read first: every node must come back as a number with good quality and a timestamp, for this configuration.
error.equipment_kind_unsupported: A monitor of this kind needs more than a list of numbers and cannot be fed by a link.
error.opcua_not_installed: The OPC UA client is not installed on the server.
error.opcua_password_missing: The environment variable for the password is not set on the server.
st.run: Tests for several states (Grubbs, Bartlett, Fisher)
st.note: ISO 22514-8: the states are the subgroup labels, or the values of the tag you name. Bartlett and Fisher assume normal data in each state. The tests inform; you decide whether to analyse each state alone or all together.
st.bartlett: Bartlett, equal variances: χ² = {stat}, {df} degrees of freedom, p = {p}: {result}
st.fisher: Fisher, equal locations: F = {stat}, {df1} and {df2} degrees of freedom, p = {p}: {result}
val.iso: ISO/TR 11462-3: the eleven reference data sets
val.iso_note: The data sets and results of the standard are built in (read from the copy of the standard that came with this program; the standard allows the data sets to be used unchanged for validation). Every run compares data set 1 to 10 (estimators, limits of six charts, out of control situations, capability) and data set 11 (Grubbs, Bartlett, Fisher, Type 1). Where the standard contradicts its own data, the check is a known difference with the evidence in the report, not a failure. The worked examples of ISO 22514-8 are run in the same way (report sections ISO 22514-8).
val.iso_desc: Model {model}, {dist}, n = {n}, subgroup size {size}, limits {lsl} to {usl}
val.iso_last: {pass} passed, {known} known differences of the standard, {info} information, {fail} failed
analysis.limit_draft: Exact limits of the draft (chi-square, w distribution)
analysis.limit_iso7870: Factors of ISO 7870-2 (A3, B3, B4, D3, D4)
ms.title: Machine performance of the states (ISO 22514-8): Pm and Pmk
ms.note: Needs both specification limits above. The states are the subgroup labels or the tag named above. The procedure: outliers (Grubbs, repeated), the widths of the local dispersions (Bartlett, or the F-test for two states), their locations (F-test, or the t/Welch test for two states), the type of global dispersion (table 1) and Pm and Pmk (table 2). Bartlett and Fisher assume normal data in each state. Where the tests are not enough, you decide.
ms.resolution: Resolution of the measuring device (forces the variance of samples of 1 to 3 scale marks)
ms.variable: The difference of the locations varies over time (type 2 and 5)
ms.star: Largest difference to expect, Δm* (empty: the observed one)
ms.physical: An outlier is real: add its amplitude to the dispersion
ms.need_limits: Enter the lower and the upper specification limit first.
ms.type_0: one dispersion for all states (widths and locations equal, ISO 22514-3)
ms.type_1: widths equal, locations different and constant
ms.type_2: widths equal, locations different and variable
ms.type_4: widths different, locations different and constant
ms.type_5: widths different, locations different and variable
ms.outlier: Outlier taken out of state {state}: {value} (G = {g} > {crit}); amplitude Δa = {da}
ms.test_widths_fisher: Widths, F-test of the variances: F = {stat}, p = {p}: {result}
ms.summary: Difference of the extreme locations Δm = {dm}; pooled standard deviation {sigma} with {dof} degrees of freedom.
report.multistate: Include the machine performance of the states (ISO 22514-8) with the settings of the block in the analysis tab
error.multistate_needs_limits: The machine performance of the states needs both specification limits.
